topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and establishes its objectives before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and sources of predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how cancer develops through clonal evolution shaped by mutations and the conditions that permit them to produce disease.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for them
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and debate surrounding the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic exposures damage DNA through their particular chemical or physical mechanisms.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how conditions within exposed tissues influence carcinogen-driven tumour development and conclude with a summary of carcinogenic mechanisms and tissue specificity.

topics.label: Human evidence of carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how measurable evidence from humans supports the identification and assessment of carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity and mutagenicity testing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine laboratory tests used to assess carcinogenic potential and the limitations of interpreting their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by drawing together its main conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment.
